slides.text: Alpha Arena: Trading Real Crypto Alpha Arena: Trading Real Crypto - https://nof1.ai Chinese models (DeepSeek & Qwen) made money, while "Western" models lost money Benchmark was launched by AI research firm nof1 on October 17, 2025 Test AI's ability to trade cryptocurrency with real money in live markets. Six LLMs received $10K each in real money: GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok 4, DeepSeek Chat V3.1, and Qwen3 Max Each AI receives identical prompts containing real-time market data including cryptocurrency prices, technical indicators (EMA, MACD, RSI), account balances, and current holdings. The models analyze this information - and output trading decisions in JSON format. By late October, Qwen3 Max emerged as the top performer, followed by DeepSeek. All "Western" models lost money. slides.title: OpenAI converted to a for-profit - October 28,
slides.text: OpenAI converted to a for-profit - October 28, 2025 OpenAI is valued at $500 Bln: $130B (26%) - OpenAI Foundation (nonprofit, retains control) $135B (27%) - Microsoft $235B (47%) - other investors and current and former employees This conversion removes the previous equity restrictions that limited OpenAI's fundraising capabilities. Sam Altman doesn't have ownership stake in new structure. His personal wealth primarily comes from investments in major technology companies like Reddit, Stripe, and Airbnb, and numerous AI-related startups. OpenAI is A For-Profit ! SoftBank's $30B OpenAI Investment approved https://yourstory.com/ai-story/softbank-openai-investment OpenAI has committed to approximately $1.4 Trillion in infrastructure deals (computing power, data center capacity, and chip partnerships) to support OpenAI's AI infrastructure expansion Nvidia - $500B commitments with Nvidia for GPU computing power Oracle - $300B+ - computing infrastructure (4.5GW data centers) OpenAI entered a $300 billion agreement with Oracle over five years for AMD - $270B - 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs between 2026 and 2030 CoreWeave - $22.4B - AI data centers and computing infra Broadcom - Multibillion-dollar (10 GW) - develop and deploy custom AI chips designed by OpenAI, with Broadcom handling development, manufacturing, and deployment Stargate Project - $500B over 4 years (recently expanded to ~7 GW). The project includes equity funding from SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX, with SoftBank handling financial responsibility and OpenAI managing operations OpenAI planning for an IPO at up to $1 Trillion in late 2026 The IPO would fund massive AI infrastructure investments as demand grows.

slides.title: AI Updates 1 MiniMax-M2 model Open-Source Released 26-27
slides.text: AI Updates 1 MiniMax-M2 model Open-Source Released 26-27 October, Minimax - Chinese AI company Designed for agents and coding workflows Open source (MIT license ) - Hugging Face, GitHub, and ModelScope​ 200B params, MoE (10B active). This is notably smaller than DeepSeek's V3.2 (37B active) or Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 (32B active) Coding: end-to-end dev. workflows, use from all popular AI Agents Handles complex, long-chain tool-calling tasks, coordinating Shell, Browser, Python interpreter, and MCP tools Priced at only 8% of Claude Sonnet's cost while running 2x faster https://www.minimax.io/news/minimax-m2 ollama run minimax-m2:cloud Self-improving AI agents - Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM) Problem: an agent performing well in the short term doesn't necessarily lead to the best long-term improvements (a.k.a. Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch) The Huxley-Gödel Machine (research team including AI pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber ) It uses metric called Clade-level Metaproductivity (CMP), inspired by T.H. Huxley's concept of clades (lineages sharing common ancestry) CMP estimates an agent's self-improvement potential by aggregating the performance of its future descendants (long term) HGM outperformed previous methods while using less time https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TCDpDXjpgPI https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.21614 https://github.com/metauto-ai/HGM Jürgen Schmidhuber

slides.title: AI Updates 8 Ripple Effect Protocol (REP) -
slides.text: AI Updates 8 Ripple Effect Protocol (REP) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16572 - paper Coordinate 100+ agents Agents share not just their decisions but also "sensitivities" - lightweight signals describing how their choices would change if environmental variables shifted REP operates through a four-step workflow where agents 1. receive messages from neighbors, 2. generate decisions with sensitivity signals, 3. aggregate neighbor sensitivities to update coordination variables 4. optionally apply consensus rules. 41-100% improvements in coordination accuracy and efficiency over traditional Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication ProtocolBench and ProtocolRouter ProtocolBench - a benchmark comparing existing agent protocols (A2A, ACP, ANP, Agora) along four axes: task success, latency, message overhead, and robustness under failures ProtocolRouter - a learnable system that dynamically selects optimal protocols based on scenario requirements and runtime conditions. Reduced failure recovery time - https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17149 Amazon’s New AI Data Center For Anthropic in Indiana, US Uses 0.5 Mln AWS Trainium2 chips https://aws.amazon.com/ai/machine-learning/trainium/ Built in 1 year, consumes 2.2 GWatt, Truly Massive https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vnGC4YS36gU

slides.title: Question About Shoes Prompt: I ordered shoes from
slides.text: Question About Shoes Prompt: I ordered shoes from Amazon.  What I received was one left shoe instead of the right one and one right shoe instead of the left one. Should I exchange them? Perplexity: No, you shouldn't exchange them—you should return them for a replacement since Amazon sent you the wrong items (mismatched shoes) Grok: Yes, you should return or exchange them immediately.What you received is two mismatched shoes—a left shoe in place of the right, and a right shoe in place of the left. Even if they’re the correct size and style, they’re not a wearable pair. You can’t walk properly in two lefts or two rights (or in this case, one of each but labeled backwards). Gemini: similar response (both Flash and Pro) GPT 5, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq - similar response Cerebras: What a confusing situation. Yes, you should definitely exchange them. It seems like Amazon sent you a mismatched pair of shoes, with one left shoe from one pair and one right shoe from another pair. Claude Sonnet 4.5: Ha! That's actually perfect - you got exactly what you ordered (a pair of shoes), just in an entertainingly weird way. You have two functional shoes that should fit correctly, they're just on the "wrong" sides of the pair. You don't need to exchange them - just swap them! Put the left shoe that came in the right shoe's spot on your left foot, and vice versa. They'll fit perfectly fine. Qwen3-Max: It sounds like you received a mismatched pair—specifically, two shoes that are mirror images of what you should have gotten (e.g., both are reversed in orientation). However, in most standard shoe designs, a left shoe and a right shoe are meant to be worn on opposite feet, so if you actually received one left and one right shoe, that is a correct pair—even if they feel unusual at first. ... Try them on. If each shoe fits the correct foot comfortably and functions normally ... no exchange needed.

Give a brief answer" Perplexity: Your wine glass is upside down—the stem is at the top and what appears "sealed" is actually the base of the glass. Simply flip it over so the wide opening (currently at the bottom) faces upward, and you can use it normally to drink wine. Grok: No, it's a wine glass stem or base that's been separated—it's not functional for holding liquid. Gemini: No, you cannot use that as a wine glass. GPT 5: No — you can’t use it. DeepSeek: No. A wine glass sealed at the top and open at the bottom is functionally a closed tube. You cannot drink from it, as it cannot hold liquid—the wine would simply pour out the bottom. It is likely a decorative object. Mistral: No, you should not use a wine glass that is sealed at the top but open at the bottom. It’s likely a decorative item, not meant for drinking. Using it could be unsafe or impractical. Groq: No, you cannot Cerebras: No, you cannot Qwen3-Max: No, you cannot use it—it sounds like the description is reversed. A functional wine glass is open at the top (to drink from) and sealed (closed) at the bottom. If it's truly sealed at the top and open at the bottom, it’s not usable as a drinking vessel. Claude Sonnet 4.5: No, you can't use it normally. A wine glass sealed at the top and open at the bottom is inverted/upside-down and won't hold liquid.
